_note: Civilian naming and art, ruled 2026-08-25 while reviewing the hero-art pairs. Applied by build-heroes.mjs — a rename lives here, never as a hand-patch on gen/heroes.json, because anything patched onto a generated file dies at the next rebuild. Ids never change; names do. ALL FIVE VARIANT PAIRS ARE RULED as of 2026-08-25: lumberjack v1 · orphan-child v1 · farmer-family v1 (Farmer) · farmer-group v2 (Farmer with a Hat) · school-child v1 (School Child (female), a NEW unit — the plural School Children remains its own).

art._note: Only the SETTLED files are wired — single-version files with no v1/v2 ambiguity. The four pairs below stay unwired until each gets a variant ruling; per gen/art-conventions.json, picking a variant in an undeclared folder is a ruling, not a guess.

newUnits._note12: THE TWELVE PAINTED CIVILIANS, ruled 2026-09-04. Angela: "The specialties are the same for all of them. The specialty options for civilians right now, but go ahead and build the 12. I do not know the names. The names are defined inside of units and encounters." NAMES ARE PROPOSALS, NOT RULINGS: units and encounters name civilians by ARCHETYPE (Farmer, Librarian, Cook, Blacksmith, Militia, Bard), never by a personal name, so these twelve follow that convention and are named for what they are. The art slugs (apothecary-wren, sage-orla, ...) are the art chat placeholders and survive only as the art directory and the id. ONE COLLISION: specialty.militia would have produced a second hero called "Militia" beside hero.fixed.militia, so this one is "Village Militia"; "Village Archer" likewise avoids reading as a Ranger. Ids are hero.fixed.* rather than the published hero.base.civilian-* family BECAUSE path base is the Eve draft pool and civilians are not drafted — "Civilians do not have unique names. They are not drafted in that same way." Say the word and they move.

levelTables._note: Which civilian TYPE table a civilian levels on, ruled 2026-09-03. The tables live in gen/levels.json under civilianTypes; this only says who points at one. Several heroes may name the same table — that is how a group of farmers stays one curve, and how a new civilian costs one line. A civilian with no entry here levels on the class.civilian table. NOT ASSIGNED, on purpose: the eight 'aspiring' civilians, who are on their way to a real class and should not be pinned to a civilian curve; and Wife #3, Wife #5, Living Ghost and Zombie Bride, which no archetype fitted and which want a call rather than a guess. 2026-09-03, second pass: the four unassigned civilians are assigned. Wife #3 and Wife #5 both take civilian.wife; Living Ghost takes civilian.ghost; Zombie Bride takes civilian.revenant — "invent a table for Wife #3, Living Ghost, and Zombie Bride." Wife #5 was NOT named in that ruling but is the same unit kind as Wife #3, so it is pointed at the same table; flag if that is wrong. The 8 hero.aspiring.* civilians are still deliberately unassigned — they are the tutorial ladder, not roster civilians.

heroBadge._note: Ruled 2026-09-04 (engine/DECISIONS.md, "Deathbed Fighting, REVERSED"), verbatim: "There is a badge that all heroes start with. That is invisible on a hero called Hero. It is not on civilians unless expressly said so. Only those with the badge Hero bleed out. A civilian who goes down and doesn't have the hero badge is just dead and a corpse." EMPTY IS THE ANSWER TODAY — not an oversight. No civilian has been named, so every civilian that falls is dead and a corpse with no Deathbed roll and no bleed-out. Add an id here the moment one is ruled otherwise.

weapons._note: Ruled 2026-09-05 (Angela), verbatim: "every civilian should have a dagger or a knife or a pitchfork or a pile of rocks if they're a child. Really, nothing is supposed to be fielded without attacks. Everybody's supposed to have punch, which I don't think has been added. And then, really, every civilian should have some kind of weapon." Applied to EVERY class.civilian hero that does not already carry a weapon — a rule, not a list, so a civilian authored tomorrow is armed too. A civilian that already carries one keeps it (the Lumberjack keeps his axe, the Farmer his pitchfork). The pick is by LEVEL TABLE, because the table is what already says what kind of person this is. Everything not named below takes the dagger, which is the 'or a knife' of the ruling. SOFT: nobody has priced a civilian holding a dagger against one holding rocks.

placedKit._note: Ruled 2026-10-03 (engine DECISIONS.md 'every civilian fields its kit by default when an encounter places it'), Andrew: "Yes, all of the civilians, by default, should field their kit the first time they're loaded. So all of them should get it." and "If enemies have weapons assigned, they need them also when they come into play." A rule, not a list: every unit an encounter places (a setup unit or a scheduled arrival, civilian or enemy) fields the kit its row carries; the engine's one assembler does it (fix.civilians-field-kit), and nothing is read from here. The opt-in list that stood here from 2026-10-02 (placedWithKit: hero.fixed.orphans, hero.fixed.school-teacher - "The Orphanage, Orphanage, and the school teacher should start with a knife each.") is retired by it: those two field their Dagger as every placed civilian now fields its kit.
